title: What is left when seven numbers are shared out?
description: Each of seven numbers is split into tens and ones. The tens leave nothing over, so the ones digit gives the remainder for ten, five and two, and one number is built back to check.
teaching_notes: One idea: tens leave nothing when divided by ten, five or two, so only the ones digit makes a remainder. Watch for students who divide the whole number instead of reading the ones digit.

video_script.why: The child sees that the tens leave nothing over, reads the ones digit of each number, and finds the remainder for ten, five and two from it.
video_script.substitution: Split the number into tens and ones, drop the tens, and divide the ones digit by ten, five and two.
video_script.anchor: a row of seven number cards under three columns headed 10, 5 and 2, each card split into tens and ones
video_script.payoff_line: The ones digit decides every remainder

final_answer.spoken: seventy eight leaves eight, three and zero; ninety nine leaves nine, four and one; one hundred and seventy three leaves three, three and one; five hundred and seventy two leaves two, two and zero; nine hundred and eighty leaves zero, zero and zero; one thousand one hundred and eleven leaves one, one and one; two thousand three hundred and forty five leaves five, zero and one

maths_rules: one ten = 1 ten = 2 fives = 5 twos, so the tens leave nothing over for 10, 5 and 2
78: ones digit 8; 8 = 0 x 10 + 8, 8 = 1 x 5 + 3, 8 = 4 x 2 + 0; remainders 8, 3, 0
video_script.design: One idea: tens leave nothing, so the ones digit gives the remainders. Callback to the six tens of eight thousand five hundred and sixty being a whole number of tens. Wrong idea: none is broken. The row of seven cards stays on the board to the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about remainders.
<bookmark mark='list'/>The first numbers are seventy eight, ninety nine, and one hundred and seventy three.
<bookmark mark='more'/>The next are five hundred and seventy two, and nine hundred and eighty.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Last come one thousand one hundred and eleven, and two thousand three hundred and forty five.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is left over when each is divided by ten, by five and by two?

beats.on_screen: the row of cards holds still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 12 counters in groups of 5 make 2 groups with 2 counters left over; the label remainder

marks.group: twelve counters are put into groups of five
marks.left: the two counters left over are circled and named remainder

narration: <bookmark mark='group'/>Twelve counters in groups of five make two groups.
<bookmark mark='left'/>The two counters left over are called the remainder.

marks.given: the seven numbers and the three divisors are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, seven numbers, and the divisors ten, five and two.

beats.on_screen: To find: the remainder for each number and each divisor

marks.find: the words remainder for each number and divisor are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the remainder for each number and each divisor.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, tens leave nothing: a ten is 1 ten, 2 fives and 5 twos, so only the ones digit matters

marks.ones: the ones digit of each card lights up

narration: <bookmark mark='ten'/>Step one, split each number into tens and ones. A ten is one ten, two fives and five twos, so the tens leave nothing over.
<bookmark mark='ones'/>Only the ones digit can leave a remainder.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 78 ends in 8: 8, 3, 0; 99 ends in 9: 9, 4, 1; 173 ends in 3: 3, 3, 1

marks.seven: the ones digit 8 of 78 is divided by 10, 5 and 2 and the remainders 8, 3, 0 appear
marks.ninety: the ones digit 9 of 99 is divided and the remainders 9, 4, 1 appear
marks.hund: the ones digit 3 of 173 is divided and the remainders 3, 3, 1 appear

narration: <bookmark mark='seven'/>Step two, take seventy eight. Its ones digit is eight. Ten leaves eight, five leaves three, and two leaves zero.
<bookmark mark='ninety'/>Ninety nine ends in nine. Ten leaves nine, five leaves four, and two leaves one.
<bookmark mark='hund'/>One hundred and seventy three ends in three. Ten leaves three, five leaves three, and two leaves one.

marks.five: the ones digit 2 of 572 is divided by 10, 5 and 2 and the remainders 2, 2, 0 appear
marks.nine: the ones digit 0 of 980 is divided and the remainders 0, 0, 0 appear

narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Step three, take five hundred and seventy two. It ends in two. Ten leaves two, five leaves two, and two leaves zero.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>Nine hundred and eighty ends in zero, so all three leave zero.

marks.one: the ones digit 1 of 1111 is divided by 10, 5 and 2 and the remainders 1, 1, 1 appear
marks.two: the ones digit 5 of 2345 is divided and the remainders 5, 0, 1 appear

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step four, take one thousand one hundred and eleven. It ends in one, so all three leave one.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Two thousand three hundred and forty five ends in five. Ten leaves five, five leaves zero, and two leaves one.

marks.check: the number 173 is built back from tens with its remainder 3
marks.more: 173 is built back from fives and then from twos, with a tick after each line

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check one number by building it back. Seventeen tens and three make it.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Thirty four fives and three make it too. Eighty six twos and one make it as well.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The ones digit decides every remainder.
Reading across ten, five and two, seventy eight leaves eight, three and zero.
Ninety nine leaves nine, four and one.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>One hundred and seventy three leaves three, three and one.
Five hundred and seventy two leaves two, two and zero.
<bookmark mark='fives'/>Nine hundred and eighty leaves zero, zero and zero.
<bookmark mark='end'/>One thousand one hundred and eleven leaves one, one and one.
Two thousand three hundred and forty five leaves five, zero and one.
